concepts.title: Locker Puzzle and Factor Parity
concepts.definition: In the queen's puzzle each person toggles the lockers numbered as multiples of their assigned number, so a locker is toggled once for every factor of its number; it ends open exactly when its number has an odd count of factors, which happens only for square numbers where one factor pairs with itself.
concepts.formula: open_locker = (number of factors is odd) i.e. locker number is a square
concepts.key_idea: Factors come in partner pairs; only a self-paired factor (as in 4 = 2 x 2) leaves an odd count.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp101.txt lines 11-89 (locker story and factor discussion)
question_patterns: find which locker numbers remain open after all 100 people take their turn
explain why locker 6 is closed at the end of the toggling process
how many times is locker 12 toggled in the puzzle
which five lockers are touched exactly twice and give the passcode
why do only square numbered lockers stay open in the locker puzzle
determine whether locker 36 ends open or closed and justify

solution_steps.action: list the factors of the locker number
solution_steps.explain: Each person numbered by a factor toggles the locker once, so the toggle count equals the factor count.
Each factor pairs with the co-factor whose product gives the locker number, e.g. for 6: (1,6) and (2,3).
Only when the number is a square does one factor pair with itself, making the factor count odd, so the locker stays open.

concepts.title: Square Numbers
concepts.definition: A number expressible as a product of a number with itself is a square number; the squares of natural numbers are perfect squares, and their unit digits can only be 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9, so a number ending in 2, 3, 7 or 8 can never be a square.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply a number by itself to get its square; the units digit test can reject but not confirm squares.
question_patterns: find the square of 24
calculate the area of a square with side 13 units
what is 15 squared
can a perfect square end with digit 8 - justify
which of the given numbers are perfect squares by checking units digits
how many zeros will the square of a number ending in two zeros have

solution_steps.explain: The square of n is n multiplied by n, written n2.

concepts.title: Squares as Sums of Consecutive Odd Numbers
concepts.definition: Adding consecutive odd numbers beginning at 1 produces the square numbers in order, because the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared; the nth odd number equals 2n - 1, and a natural number is a perfect square only if repeated subtraction of 1, 3, 5, ... reaches exactly 0.
concepts.key_idea: Each square grows by the next odd number: 1, 1+3, 1+3+5, ... give 1, 4, 9, ...
question_patterns: find 36 squared given that 35 squared is 1225 using odd numbers
what is the 36th odd number
check whether 38 is a perfect square by subtracting consecutive odd numbers
express 25 as a sum of successive odd numbers
calculate the sum of the first 6 odd numbers and identify the square
how many odd numbers starting from 1 must be added to reach 64

solution_steps.explain: The odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, ...; the nth term is 2n minus 1.

solution_steps.action: add it to the previous square
solution_steps.explain: Since the first n odd numbers sum to n squared, the new square equals the previous one plus the nth odd number.

concepts.title: Square Roots
concepts.definition: If y = x squared then x is the square root of y; every perfect square carries two integer roots, one positive and one negative, and this chapter works with the positive root. Roots can be found by pairing prime factors, by subtracting successive odd numbers, or by estimating between known squares.
concepts.key_idea: Square root undoes squaring: area of a square gives its side through the root.
concepts.textbook_ref: hegp101.txt lines 299-338 (square root), 390-450 (prime factor pairing, estimation), 451-479 (estimating 250 and 125)
question_patterns: find the side of a square whose area is 49 sq cm
calculate the square root of 576 using prime factorisation
estimate the square root of 250 to the nearest integer
is 156 a perfect square - justify using prime factors
what is the largest integer-sided square handkerchief that fits in cloth of area 125 sq cm
find the length of the side of a square whose area is 441 sq m

solution_steps.action: take the positive square root of the area
solution_steps.explain: The side of the square is the positive root of its area.

concepts.title: Cubic Numbers
concepts.definition: Numbers obtained by multiplying a number by itself three times are cubic numbers, called perfect cubes when n is a natural number; a cube of edge n holds n x n x n unit cubes, and cubes of fractions and decimals follow the same triple product.
concepts.key_idea: Cube means three self-multiplications: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8, 3 x 3 x 3 = 27.
question_patterns: find the cube of 12
how many unit cubes make a cube of side 4 units
calculate 15 cubed
is 9 a perfect cube - justify
what is the volume of a cube with edge 6 cm
compute the cube of 13.08

solution_steps.action: multiply the number by itself twice
solution_steps.explain: The cube of n is n times n times n, written n3.

concepts.title: Taxicab Numbers (Hardy-Ramanujan Number)
concepts.definition: Numbers expressible as a sum of two positive cubes in two different ways are taxicab numbers; 1729 is the smallest, made famous by Ramanujan's reply to Hardy, followed by 4104 and 13832.
question_patterns: why is 1729 called the Hardy-Ramanujan number
express 1729 as a sum of two cubes in two different ways
what is a taxicab number - define it
find the two ways of writing 4104 as a sum of two positive cubes
which number did Ramanujan call very interesting and why

solution_steps.explain: Check 1 and 12 give 1 + 1728, while 9 and 10 give 729 + 1000; both totals are 1729.
The two pairs of cubes are distinct, which is exactly the taxicab property.
